title: Can LLMs Access their World Knowledge for Event Prediction?
abstract: arXiv:2610.19021v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent work has questioned whether large language models (LLMs) can be useful for temporal event prediction. Despite vast pretrained world knowledge, LLMs often underperform simpler specialized models. We ask whether this knowledge is truly inaccessible, or whether current methods fail to present event prediction in a form LLMs can use. We argue for the latter and show that LLMs become effective event forecasters when the interface is designed around two choices. The first grounds each event in a natural-language description, and the second separates event semantics from the prediction space to prevent semantic bias from label associations. To test this, we introduce DescribeEvent, a benchmark of ~150K events across seven datasets and six domains with event-level descriptions. translated_title: 大语言模型能否利用其世界知识进行事件预测？
translated_abstract: 近期的研究质疑大语言模型（LLM）在时间性事件预测任务上是否真的有用。尽管拥有庞大的预训练世界知识，LLM 的表现往往不如更简单的专用模型。我们探究的问题是：这种知识是否真的无法被访问，还是当前方法未能以 LLM 能够利用的形式来呈现事件预测？我们支持后一种观点，并证明当接口围绕两个设计选择来构建时，LLM 可以成为有效的事件预测器。第一个选择是将每个事件扎根于自然语言描述之中，第二个选择是将事件语义与预测空间分离，以防止标签关联带来的语义偏差。为了验证这一点，我们推出了 DescribeEvent，一个包含约 15 万个事件、横跨七个数据集和六个领域、并带有事件级描述的基准测试。我们发现，能力较强的 LLM 从描述和符号化标签中显著受益，超越了无描述的变体以及非 LLM 基线，而较弱的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出通过“自然语言事件描述”和“将事件语义与符号化预测标签分离”的接口设计，让 LLM 有效调用其世界知识进行事件预测，并推出包含约 15 万事件、横跨七个数据集和六个领域的 DescribeEvent 基准验证了该方法优于无描述变体和非 LLM 基线。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that LLMs can effectively access their world knowledge for event prediction when the interface grounds events in natural-language descriptions and separates event semantics from symbolic prediction labels, validated by the new DescribeEvent benchmark of ~150K events across seven datasets and six domains, outperforming description-free variants and non-LLM baselines.
